ceviri.20: Does an app built with React Native lag behind a native app on performance?
ceviri.21: Because the interface components bind to the platform's own native components, there's no noticeable difference in everyday use. In the rare cases needing heavy graphics or complex animation, that module is moved to native code and the performance gap is closed.
ceviri.22: Why choose React Native rather than Flutter?
ceviri.23: Flutter also offers a single codebase, but it uses the Dart language, which doesn't overlap with your web team's React knowledge. With React Native the same team can share component logic, so the project stays more efficient.
ceviri.24: What's the advantage of using the same API as our website?
ceviri.25: Data such as products, users and orders is defined in one place on the server; web and mobile call the same endpoints. That removes the job of keeping two separate data sources in step — an update on one side shows automatically on the other.
ceviri.26: How does a React Native app get submitted to both stores?
ceviri.27: The shared codebase is put through platform-specific build steps to produce separate iOS and Android packages, and an automated release pipeline gets them ready for submission.
ceviri.28: On which projects does React Native fall short and native become necessary?
ceviri.29: On projects with heavy sensor processing or highly platform-specific graphics requirements, that module may need writing in native code; the rest of the app can stay on React Native.
ceviri.30: Can an app built with React Native be moved to native later?
ceviri.31: Yes — when the architecture is built in modules, screens or features can be moved to native code one at a time. Because the move can be gradual, the parts that need it can be shifted to native over time without interrupting the existing app.

ceviri.49: Mobile App Development with React Native
ceviri.50: With React Native we build your iOS and Android app from a single codebase and have it share the same API infrastructure as your website, delivering data consistency and development efficiency together.
ceviri.51: Let's map the scope and price range
ceviri.63: One Codebase, Two Stores, a Shared API Layer
ceviri.64: On React Native projects the iOS and Android interfaces are produced from the same JavaScript/TypeScript codebase; the code branches only where platform-specific behaviour is needed, and the rest of the logic stays shared.
ceviri.65: The real value of this structure shows when the mobile app consumes the same API as your website: the product catalogue, user accounts, orders or booking logic are defined in one place on the server, and the web and mobile clients pull that logic from the same endpoints. Stock levels, price updates and user permissions stay consistent and in step across every channel. The sharing isn't limited to the interface layer either; validation rules and some business logic functions can be shared between web and mobile too.
ceviri.67: React Native or Flutter: Why Do We Lean Towards React Native?
ceviri.68: Flutter also releases to two platforms from one codebase, but it uses the Dart language and its own render engine — which means a team using React and JavaScript on the web can't reuse that knowledge on mobile.
ceviri.69: That's our reason for choosing React Native: the same team building your web interface can carry the component logic straight across to mobile. Mature libraries in the npm ecosystem solve common needs like authentication or payments with ready-made modules. Because the architecture binds directly to native components, the interface behaves close to the platform's own. On projects running web and mobile at the same time, the code and knowledge sharing React Native gives you comes to the fore. A single codebase is still subject to the store rules;

ceviri.147: If you'd like to look before deciding
ceviri.148: The Native Bridge and Third-Party Modules
ceviri.149: For device-specific capabilities such as the camera, biometric login or push notifications, React Native reaches the platform's APIs through a native bridge layer. Community modules cover most scenarios; where a bespoke hardware integration is needed, a small native module is brought in.
ceviri.150: State Management and a Scalable Project Architecture
ceviri.151: As an app grows, managing the flow of data between screens becomes critical. We set up a layered folder structure with type safety through TypeScript, along with central state management; API calls and error handling are gathered in a separate service layer.
ceviri.152: CI/CD and the Store Release Pipeline
ceviri.153: We set up a CI/CD pipeline that automates the build, signing and store upload steps; every release goes through the same checks, and parallel submission to both stores becomes routine.

_kararlar.103-106 / 86-91 / 111 tekrar eden dizgel: SVG kartlarında aynı Türkçe dizge birden çok kez geçiyor: 'tek kod' (103,105), 'tabanı' (104,106), 'gerektiğinde' (86,90) ve 'native' (87,91,111). Değişim global olduğu için her Türkçe dizgeye TEK karşılık verilebilir — çakışma kilidi durdurdu. 'native' 111'de özellik etiketi olarak da geçiyor ('native bileşenler'), bu yüzden karşılığı 'native' olmak ZORUNDA; nitelemeyi üst satır taşıyor: 'if needed' / 'native'. 'tek kod tabanı' iki kartta da 'one' / 'codebase' olarak bölündü.
_kararlar.113-114 iki platforma / yayın: Türkçede sıra 'iki platforma → yayın', İngilizcede 'release to → two platforms'. Kayıt sırası korunduğu için satırlar da doğru sırada okunuyor.
_kararlar.67 Tercih neden React Native'den yana: 'Why We Lean Towards React Native'. Türkçedeki tercih beyanı korundu; 'Why React Native Wins' iddialı olurdu ve sayfanın kendi tarafsızlık notuyla çelişirdi.
_kararlar.117 temsilî görsel notu: Kritik: iki kartın EŞİT ölçüde olduğunu, Flutter maddelerinin sayfanın kendi ifadeleri olduğunu ve kıyasın 'bir puan ya da ölçüm değil, tercih gerekçesinin gösterimi' olduğunu söylüyor. Bu beyan birebir aktarıldı — yumuşatmak ya da atlamak sayfayı Flutter aleyhine ölçüm iddia eder hâle getirirdi.
_kararlar.148 native köprü (bridge): Sektör terimi; Türkçe metin parantezle İngilizcesini zaten veriyor, İngilizcede tek terim yeterli ('a native bridge layer').
_kararlar.58-59 sayaç etiketleri: KOD TABANI/MAĞAZA → CODEBASE/STORES. 'Mağaza' tekil ama iki mağaza sayılıyor; İngilizcede çoğul doğal (iOS+Android sayfasındaki PLATFORMS/LANGUAGES kararıyla tutarlı).
